Hi Jason —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from the demo focused on reranking and how Redwood would integrate into PebbleHealth's search stack: 

What we covered:
- High-level flow: query -> candidate retrieval (existing DB) -> embeddings similarity -> Redwood reranker (seq2seq model) -> final score + structured output for UI prioritization.
- Constraints you mentioned: 150ms p95 latency target for reranker on top-50 candidate lists; HIPAA-aware hosting (Private deployment preferred); and the need for audit logs for scoring decisions.

Immediate asks / next steps we promised:
1) Share a short integration checklist (SDK auth, routing, sample payloads) — attached as "pebble-post-demo-notes.pdf" and "pebble-architecture.png".
2) Confirm auth approach: service-account scoped API keys vs. per-user tokens.
3) Provide representative sample queries + relevance labels (if available) so we can propose an offline eval plan.
4) Agree target top_k and candidate pool sizes to scope latency testing.

Can you confirm who on your side will own sharing the dataset and whether we can get a small sample (100–200 queries with ground-truth ranks)? Once we have that, Ben and Aisha will sketch an offline eval and a simple live pilot runbook.

Proposed timeline:
- Dataset & auth decision: by end of week (8/13)
- Offline eval plan and baseline results: +1 week after dataset
- Pilot rollout (canary): week of 8/30

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—

Laura — thanks for the clear recap. A few technical questions from our side before we assemble the dataset: 

1) Auth & secrets: We prefer service-account scoped keys managed in our org KMS. Is there an option for short-lived tokens issued by Redwood using our OIDC provider (we want rotating credentials, not long-lived API keys).

2) SDK/host: We'll likely run Redwood Private in our VPC. Which SDKs do you recommend for orchestration (we currently use Python + Node microservices)? Any guidance for in-cluster routing to avoid egress costs?

3) Latency: 150ms p95 seems aggressive for reranker over top-50 if the model is large. Can you outline expected latency ranges for your verified models for top-10, top-25, top-50? Also curious about strategies (quantization, async scoring, cache priming) you suggest.

4) Evaluation metrics: we typically use NDCG and MRR, but we want guidance on slice-level metrics (e.g., recency bias, clinical-term matches). Do you have a suggested signal matrix?

We'll pull together ~200 anonymized queries with labels by EOW if that works. Could your team provide a minimal eval harness (script/notebook) that we can run internally?

Thanks — Jason

Laura / Aisha —
Quick draft answers and recommended config to send Jason: 

Auth / tokens:
- Recommendation: OIDC-based short-lived tokens minted by Pebble's identity provider + JWKS validation on the Redwood Private control plane. This avoids long-lived API keys and integrates with KMS rotation policies. We can provide a small auth proxy snippet we run as a sidecar to mint/refresh tokens — attached as "auth-snippet.py".

SDKs / routing:
- SDKs: Python and Node are first-class (we also support Java). For in-cluster routing to avoid egress, use our local sidecar that routes calls to the private inference nodes over the VPC/internal load balancer.
- Routing policy: recommend primary route -> dedicated reranker pool (quantized) with fallback to a smaller, faster model if p95 latency exceeds SLO.

Latency expectations (ballpark for verified models on a 40 GB GPU in Private):
- Top-10 scoring (seq2seq reranker, 512 token context): ~40–70ms median, 110–160ms p95 depending on model size and batch behavior.
- Top-25: ~70–120ms median, 150–260ms p95.
- Top-50: ~120–240ms median, 260–480ms p95.
Notes: latency tightness depends on batch size and caching. For strict 150ms p95 we suggest restricting live reranker to top-25 and doing asynchronous background rescoring for larger pools.

Top_k tuning / caching:
- Start with top_k=25 for live; use offline eval to compare NDCG@10/25. Use prefix/KV cache priming for repeated queries and short-circuit identical candidate embeddings.

Offline eval plan (attach: "rerank-eval-plan.md"):
- Inputs: candidates (IDs), query text, ground-truth ranks/labels (binary or graded).
- Metrics: NDCG@10/25, MRR, Recall@k, pairwise AUC. Include slice metrics (recency, clinical-term match rate).
- Pilot steps: baseline with current ranking -> run Redwood reranker -> compute deltas and run small human blind eval on 200 samples.

I'll attach a minimal Python SDK snippet and an evaluation notebook we can hand to Jason.

Attachments: rerank-eval-plan.md, auth-snippet.py

—

Looping Jason in — quick note on evaluation signals and next steps from an ML perspective: 

Suggested offline metric suite:
- Primary: NDCG@10 (captures ranking quality at top of list)
- Secondary: MRR, Recall@k (k=25), and pairwise loss for model training diagnostics
- Slice metrics: recency (last 30d), clinical-term precision (domain-specific lexicon), click-to-action lift (if click logs available)

Evaluation plan (short):
1) Run baseline scoring on their sample set (we'll provide a small harness) -> compute metrics.
2) Train/quantize a candidate reranker variant (if needed) -> produce offline rerank outputs.
3) Compute NDCG deltas and surface worst-performing slices for annotation.
4) If deltas look good, run a 1% live canary with top_k=25 for 2 weeks and collect online signals.

Data needs from Pebble:
- 200 anonymized queries with graded labels (or implicit labels + click logs)
- Candidate pools (top-50 IDs per query) and embedding vectors if you want to run local sim comparisons

I'll schedule a 30-minute technical workshop with Ben and Jason to walk through the eval harness and auth flow. Proposed slots: Wed 8/11 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 8/12 14:00–14:30 PT. Jason — which works best for you?

Thanks — Aisha
